title: Alpha Drops Its Teaser Today. The YRF Spy Universe Finally Has Its Most Dangerous Women.
excerpt: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari star as elite assassins in the franchise's first female-led origin story — with Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan rumoured to make an appearance.
body:
The YRF Spy Universe has given us Pathaan, Tiger, and Kabir. It's given us car chases through European capitals, gunfights on moving trains, and Hrithik Roshan looking like he was carved from Italian marble. What it hasn't given us — until now — is a woman who gets to run the whole operation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8zqfxQcz7kM

That changes today.

Alpha, the Alia Bhatt and Sharvari-led spy thriller from Yash Raj Films, drops its first teaser on June 10 — and everything about the rollout suggests Aditya Chopra is treating this like the most important Spy Universe entry since Pathaan. The teaser will reveal the origin story of a girl raised and built to become a killing machine — a premise that marks a franchise first: an assassin's origin, not a mission briefing.

Directed by Shiv Rawail, whose The Railway Men proved he could handle both scale and tension with a steady hand, Alpha positions Alia and Sharvari as elite agents in a narrative the makers describe as being about "attitude, not just action." A senior trade source put it plainly: the campaign is designed to make "Alpha" synonymous with a generation of women who refuse to be limited.

"Alpha's campaign is built around the core idea that Alpha is more than a character or a film title — it is an attitude." — Senior trade source

It's a big swing. But then, the casting alone makes the case. Alia has been one of Bollywood's most bankable leads for years — from Gangubai Kathiawadi to Jigra, she's proven she can carry raw intensity without losing an ounce of vulnerability. Sharvari, coming off a career-defining stretch with Munjya and Vedaa, brings a physicality and coiled screen presence that the Spy Universe badly needs if it wants to evolve beyond its boys' club. Together, they're being positioned as the franchise's new centre of gravity.

Rounding out the cast are Bobby Deol — riding a villainous renaissance that started with Animal and hasn't slowed down — and Anil Kapoor, adding the kind of veteran gravitas that the Spy Universe loves to deploy in its layered operative roles. No specifics on their characters yet, but the franchise has a habit of turning its supporting cast into scene-stealing assets.

The Shah Rukh Khan Question

It wouldn't be a Spy Universe film without cameo speculation, and Alpha has had its share. Reports from late 2025 suggested that Chopra approached Shah Rukh Khan to reprise Pathaan for a special sequence — one designed to bridge Alpha directly into Pathaan 2. SRK reportedly asked for time to decide. Meanwhile, Hrithik Roshan is rumoured to appear as agent Kabir, his War character, which would make Alpha the most interconnected entry in the franchise's history.

Neither cameo has been officially confirmed. But the possibilities alone are enough to make this teaser one of the most anticipated reveals of the year. If even one of them materialises, Alpha stops being a standalone expansion and becomes the connective tissue for the entire universe.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences who've tracked the Spy Universe's evolution from Ek Tha Tiger into a genuine cinematic franchise, Alpha represents something significant: the first real expansion beyond the male-dominated template that defined the series. The July 3 release date puts it squarely in the summer window — prime diaspora season, when families are most likely to make it to theatres together.

YRF has planned what insiders describe as a "relentless" post-teaser campaign: trailers, character drops, digital activations, and youth-focused engagements rolling out in "carefully calibrated phases" through June. Expect Alia and Sharvari to be everywhere. Expect the conversation to be about something bigger than just another spy film.

The teaser drops today. The attitude arrives July 3.
